newsitem.title: USA: Foxmeyer Drug liquidation approved by court.
newsitem.headline: Foxmeyer Drug liquidation approved by court.

text.p: Foxmeyer Drug Co., once one of the largest wholesale drug distributors in the United States, won court approval Tuesday to begin liquidating the company under federal bankruptcy law.

U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Helen Balick approved a measure for Foxmeyer and five affiliates to convert their Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings to Chapter 7. Under Chapter 7, a liquidation trustee will be appointed to prepare a plan to distribute the company's assets to its creditors.
Foxmeyer, which had revenue of more than $5 billion in 1996, filed for reorganization under Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings last August.

It sold substantially all business operations and related assets to McKesson Corp. in November after being "forced (to) by mounting business problems and rapidly escalating financial losses," according to court papers.
Foxmeyer said monthly administration costs as high as $2 million and a pending lawsuit were among the factors for converting to Chapter 7.
It said a liquidation trustee would be "a central source of control" for reducing costs and managing litigation.
"The debtors believe a conversion will serve the best interests of their estates, creditors and stockholders and will not prejudice the rights of any party in these cases," court papers said.
The five affiliates are Foxmeyer Corp., HealthCare Transportation System Inc., Merchandise Coordinator Services Corp., FoxMeyer Software Inc., and HealthMart Inc.
